title: Finding Counterfactual Evidences for Node Classification

problem.claim: Search for counterfactual evidences in GNN-based node classification.

gap.claim: Randomized controlled trials are often impractical, so counterfactual detection must rely on available observational factual data.

contributions.claim: Effective and efficient algorithms for searching for counterfactual evidences.
An indexing solution using node features and structural information to identify counterfactual evidences.
Downstream applications use counterfactual evidences to address fairness and accuracy of GNNs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the indexing solution as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrating the potential of counterfactual evidences to enhance fairness and accuracy through various downstream applications.

narrative_sequence.summary: Counterfactual learning is presented as a causality-rooted paradigm addressing fairness and interpretability issues in GNNs.
Because randomized controlled trials may be impractical, observational factual data are needed to detect counterfactuals.
The paper formulates searching for counterfactual evidences in GNN-based node classification.
It defines counterfactual evidences as similarly featured and structured node pairs receiving different GNN classifications, then proposes search algorithms and indexing.
Downstream applications are reported to show potential benefits for GNN fairness and accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Pairs of nodes with similar features and neighborhood structures but different GNN classifications can serve as counterfactual evidences.

interpretation.claim: Structured disagreement among similar graph instances can expose possible classification weaknesses.

application.claim: Use such evidence to investigate or improve fairness and accuracy in GNN-based node classification.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that every such disagreement indicates a causal effect or a confirmed model defect.
